clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old woman presented with a two-week history of mild headache followed by one week of double vision. On examination, she had severe bilateral papilledema with obliterated disc margins and bilateral abducens nerve palsy, with no fever or meningeal signs. Lumbar puncture revealed markedly elevated opening pressure (>50 cm H2O) with CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis (188 WBC/mm3, 88% lymphocytes), elevated protein (117.60 mg/dl), and low glucose (2 mmol/L). MRI brain showed signs of elevated intracranial pressure including distended optic nerve sheath, flattened globe at the disc, partially empty sella, and bilateral transverse sinus narrowing without venous thrombosis. Brucella serology (Rose Bengal test) was positive with Brucella melitensis 2ME titer of 1:320. CSF culture on day 7 of admission grew Brucella melitensis, confirming the diagnosis of neurobrucellosis. She was treated with ceftriaxone 2g IV twice daily (4 weeks), rifampicin 600mg PO daily (12 weeks), doxycycline 100mg PO twice daily, and acetazolamide 500mg three times daily for intracranial pressure management. By 4-week follow-up, headache and double vision had resolved. By 10-week follow-up, papilledema had completely resolved, and acetazolamide was tapered off.
